cards.title: Saving water at home
facts: A running tap can waste several litres a minute.
RO purifiers reject a lot of water that can be reused for mopping or plants.
A bucket bath usually uses far less water than a shower.
do: Turn off the tap while brushing
Reuse RO reject water for mopping or plants
Water plants early in the morning
dont: Don't wash vehicles with a running hose

myths.statement: A small dripping tap wastes too little water to matter.
myths.truth: Drips add up to thousands of litres a year. Fix or report it.

quiz.q: Which saves the most water every day?
options: Leaving the tap on while brushing
Turning the tap off while brushing
Washing the car with a hose
quiz.explanation: Small daily habits save a lot over a year.

situations: It's a dry summer in {name}'s city and water comes only twice a day. {At}, {relation} is washing a scooter with a hose that's been running for 20 minutes.
scenario.question: What could {name} suggest?

rubric.point: Use a bucket instead of a running hose
rubric.note: A bucket uses a fraction of the water.

rubric.point: Reuse water (e.g. RO reject) where possible

cards.title: Heat and air quality days
facts: On high-AQI days, hard outdoor exercise means breathing in more pollution.
Burning leaves and waste adds smoke directly to the air.
The hottest part of the day is usually around noon to 3 PM.
do: Check the AQI before outdoor sport
Avoid hard exercise outdoors when AQI is high
Share rides or use public transport
dont: Don't do hard outdoor exercise at midday in a heatwave

myths.statement: If the sky looks clear, the air quality must be good.
myths.truth: Fine particles (PM2.5) are invisible. Check the AQI.

quiz.q: The AQI is 210 today. What's the best choice for sports practice?
options: Move practice indoors or make it light
Burn leaves to clear the air
quiz.explanation: High AQI means more pollution in your lungs during hard exercise.

cards.title: Wet, dry and hazardous waste
facts: Wet waste (food, peels) can be composted.
Batteries and e-waste contain harmful chemicals and need special disposal.
do: Separate wet, dry and hazardous waste
Give e-waste and batteries to collection points
dont: Don't throw batteries in the regular bin

myths.statement: Old batteries can go in the kitchen bin with everything else.
myths.truth: Batteries are hazardous waste. Use e-waste or battery collection points.

quiz.explanation: Food scraps are wet waste and can be composted.

cards.title: Saving energy at home
facts: Setting the AC to 24–26°C saves a lot of electricity compared with 18–20°C.
Chargers and devices on standby still use some power.
do: Switch off lights and fans when leaving a room
dont: Don't leave the TV on standby all night
Don't open the fridge door for long

myths.statement: Setting the AC to 16°C cools the room faster.
myths.truth: It cools at the same speed, just longer and colder, using more power. 24–26°C is efficient.

quiz.q: Which AC setting is the most energy-efficient for comfort?
